page.layout: One column of dictionary entries, with the page number at top left and the running head "R U." at top centre. The catchword "Rumor" stands at the lower right below the last line. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: Rudes ad gubernacula inepti] Remum ducat, qui nihil didicit.
Rudes loquaciores eruditis] Vacuum vas altius pleno resonat. Vasa inania tinniunt.

Ruditas morum] Rusticitas, Plin. Enormitas rusticitatis, Diomed. Barbarismus, Barbaries, Cic. Rus: plenus ruris, Cat. Merum rus, Plaut. Simplicitas rudis, Ovid. Impolitia, Gell. Inficetiæ, Infacetiæ, Catul. Atechnia, Quint.
Ruere] Ruinam dare, Virg. Facere, Hor. Corruere, Liv. Tecta super habitantes procubuerunt, Quint.
Rufus] Rutilus, Var. Russus, Apul. Ænobarbus. Homo æneâ barbâ, Suet. Æri similis capillus, Id.
Ruga ostendit senium] Facies tua computat annos.

Rugosus] Facies rugosior uvâ passâ, Claud. Rugatus. Corrugatus, Col. Striata, contracta frons, Apul. Adstricta frons, Mart. Contricta fronte Catones, Petron. Cossus, à similitudine cossi, vermis lignorum, dictus; est rugosi corporis homo, Fest.
Ruina] Demolitio statuarum. Excisio tectorum, Cic. Dejectus arborum, Plin.

Ruminare] Remandere, Plin. Revocare palearibus herbas, Calpur. Præteritos cibos in ore volvere, & in alvum missos iterum retrahere, Hieron. Pasto pasci cibo: Atque iterum pasto pascitur ante cibo, Ovid.
Rumor] Rumusculus. Aura rumoris. Fama, Cic.

Rumor est] Rumores sparsi sunt. Rumoris nescio quid afflaverat. Nihil à te ad nos rumoris affluxit. Rumor perfertur ex Asiâ. Rumore nuntio audivimus. Rumor serpit. Perfert, affert aliquid rumor. Fama est, celebrat, nunciat, surrexit, percrebuit, emanavit, ad aures meas pervenit. Fama aliquid accepi. Affertur, Absol. &, Affertur rumor, Cic. Fama fert: ita tenet; Fama traditur, perfertur, obtinet, Liv. Fama persuasit, Tac. Vulgavit, Curt. Circumfert, Plin. Crebrescit fama, Tac. Fama in vulgus exierat, Suet. vid. Adjunt.

page.notes: Faint show-through from the facing page is visible in the margins and was not transcribed. The entry "Rumor est]" is printed as one long paragraph in the original; it is kept as one.
